\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We study the ${\mathcal M}$-closed validation of a generative model $q$ against a
target $p$ over the space ${\mathcal X}$. Conformal calibration turns a weak plug-in
classifier into a powerful two-sample test with finite-sample type-I control.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
A popular tool for evaluating generative models is the classifier two-sample
test (C2ST). It reframes distributional comparison between $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ as
a classification task over the space ${\mathcal X}$, with the Bayes-optimal classifier
bisecting $\mathbb{R}^2$ between the two means.

\paragraph{Summary of contributions.} We introduce the Conformal C2ST and give
a robustness theory for weak classifiers. We show that conformal calibration
decouples type-I error control from discriminative accuracy.

\paragraph{A toy example.} Consider ${\mathcal N}(\mathbf{0}, I_2)$ versus a mean shift,
so that $q$ is ${\mathcal N}([0.5, 0]^\top, I_2)$. The rank statistic
\[
  r = \sum_{i=1}^{M} {\mathbb I}\{\theta \le \tilde\theta_i\}
\]
is uniform over $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ when $q$ matches $p$.

\section{Robustness of the uniform test}
Let ${\mathcal O}$ denote an oracle and write the conformal $p$-value as a function of
the score. We control the variance $\text{Var}[r]$ and the expectation $\mathbb{E}[r]$ of
the rank statistic under the null.

\begin{theorem}[Decoupling]
\label{thm:decouple}
For any plug-in classifier with score $s$, the conformal calibration map
satisfies
\[
  \Big| \mathbb{E}\big[ \phi(s) \big] - \alpha \Big| \le \left\| {s - s^\star} \right\|
  \xrightarrow{\;n \to \infty\;} 0 ,
\]
where $s^\star$ is the Bayes-optimal score and $\left| {\alpha} \right| \le 1$.
\end{theorem}

As shown in Theorem~\ref{thm:decouple}, the conformal test maintains validity
even when the classifier is weak, since the ranking signal
$\overset{\text{rank}}{\longrightarrow}$ aggregates across draws.

\section{Introduction}
\subsection{Legendre Polynomials}
Let $P_k(x)$ be the degree $k$ Legendre polynomial. The Legendre polynomials
are an orthogonal family of polynomials on $[-1,1]$ that obey the orthogonality
relation
$$
\int_{-1}^1 P_j(x) P_k(x) dx = 0,
$$
for $j \not = k$. The first few Legendre polynomials are
$$
P_0(x) = 1, \qquad P_1(x) = x, \qquad \text{and} \qquad P_2(x) = \frac{3 x^2 - 1}{2}.  
$$
The Legendre polynomials obey the recurrence relation
$$
(k+1) P_{k+1}(x) = (2 k + 1) x P_k(x) - k P_{k-1}(x),
$$
the differential equation
$$
(1 - x^2) P_k''(x) - 2 x P_k'(x) + k(k+1) P_k(x) = 0,
$$
for $k \ge 1$.
